title: A counselor in the Presidency serves by strengthening the weak
setting: Joseph Smith had been ordained President of the High Priesthood at Amherst, Ohio, in January 1832. On 8 March he chose Jesse Gause and Sidney Rigdon as counselors. This revelation, dated 15 March 1832 at Hiram, was first addressed to Gause. Gause did not continue faithfully and was excommunicated in December 1832. Frederick G. Williams’s name later replaced his, and Williams was ordained a counselor on 18 March 1833.
summary: The revelation calls Frederick G. Williams to be a high priest and a counselor to Joseph Smith. It says Joseph holds the keys of the kingdom, which belong to the Presidency of the High Priesthood. It promises blessings if the counselor is faithful in counsel, in prayer, and in preaching. It asks for prayer both vocally and in the heart, in public and in private. It tells him to succor the weak, lift up hands that hang down, and strengthen feeble knees. If he is faithful to the end, he will receive a crown of immortality and eternal life.

contextNote.title: What a counselor’s office is for
contextNote.text: A new office raised the question of what a counselor actually does. Verse 5 answers with action: it tells the counselor to “succor the weak” and strengthen feeble knees. Verse 3 lists the duties that come first: counsel, constant prayer, and preaching. Verse 4 says that doing these things brings “the greatest good” to others. The wording of verse 5 echoes Isaiah 35:3 and Hebrews 12:12. In this passage, to “stand in the office” means lifting others, not holding rank.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 81–83, “Much Is Given Much Is Required,” studies this call to a counselor in the Presidency. Whom could you “succor” or strengthen this week in the ways verse 5 lists?
reviewNote: Read all 7 verses. Heading gives Hiram, 15 March 1832, the change from Gause to Williams, and Williams’s 18 March 1833 ordination. JSP historical introduction gives the 25 January 1832 Amherst ordination, the 8 March appointment of Gause and Rigdon, and Gause’s December 1832 excommunication. The summary follows the current text, which names Williams. Fact-check 2026-10-12: contextNote misread verse 4 as giving the reason for verse 5’s acts; verse 4 refers back to verse 3’s duties. Reordered and corrected.
